compliance.acoustic: 27.3 / 27.1 / 36.6 dBA at 0 / 50 / 100 percent PoE load (guide Table 4); 27.1 dBA in the datasheet

environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 50 C at sea level, 0 to 45 C up to 1500 m, 0 to 40 C up to 3000 m

features.optics-sfp-plus: the two Virtual Chassis ports and the two uplink ports are 1GE or 10GE SFP+ ports (Table 15 and Figure 15 callout 2). Virtual Chassis is supported only with 10GE SFP+, and not with a 10GBASE-T transceiver in a Virtual Chassis port. Industrial-grade optics are asked for only on the fanless models
features.uplink-ports: two SFP+ ports take 1 GbE or 10 GbE transceivers
features.virtual-chassis: up to 6 EX4000 switches; the two Virtual Chassis ports are SFP+ and VC formation is not supported with a 10GBASE-T transceiver in them

management.console: RJ-45 console on the rear panel, labelled CON
management.oob: management Ethernet RJ-45 on the rear panel, with a link activity lamp and a status lamp
management.usb: one USB 2.0 Type-A port on the front panel

physical.weight-note: 10.8 lb (4.9 kg), Table 26; 4.84 kg in the datasheet

power.poe-standard: PoE+ (IEEE 802.3at) on all 48 ports, 30 W per port
power.power-input: 100 to 127 VAC at 12 A or 200 to 240 VAC at 7.5 A, 50 to 60 Hz (Table 34)

thermal.cooling: three inbuilt fixed fans, front-to-back airflow, 28 CFM (datasheet)

ac.description: The switch as shipped: 48 PoE+ ports, the built-in AC power supply and three built-in front-to-back fans. EX4000-48P is the only hardware SKU the datasheet lists for the model (Table 1 and the ordering information); there is no DC, back-to-front, -S or -TAA variant.

description: Juniper EX4000-48P, a fixed 1U access switch with 48 10/100/1000BASE-T ports that all supply PoE+ (30 W per port, 740 W budget). The front also has two SFP+ Virtual Chassis ports and two SFP+ uplink ports, a USB 2.0 Type-A port, a reset pinhole and the SYS, MST and CLD status lamps. The rear has an RJ-45 management port, an RJ-45 console port, three exhaust fans, an earthing terminal and the AC inlet. The power supply and the three fans are built into the chassis, so there are no bays. Airflow is front to back.

gaps.wanted: The brackets of EX-RMK (provided), EX-4PST-RMK and JNP-4PST-RMK-1U-E (orderable) are named in Table 5 and the mounting topics and are not modelled as kit contracts in this slice. A dimensioned drawing of the bracket fold lines would give the flush position an at.

A per-port vocabulary for the Status lamp. Table 32 gives its colour by speed (off 10 Mbps, blinking green 100 Mbps, green 1000 Mbps, amber 2.5 Gbps), which the jack's own lamp states do not carry, so the jack keeps the component's default off, link and activity states.
The size of the claim code label (Figure 15 callout 7). It is drawn as a region and not as a part, and the photograph does not show it.
The Junos interface names. The hardware guide gives the PIC numbering only inside the Junos configuration topics, which this slice does not read.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.
The diameter and depth of the pinhole reset button (Figure 15 callout 6). The guide names the button and gives no size; the hole is drawn at 2.0 mm as an estimate.

mgmt.mixed: how the switch is reached out of band and reset - the RJ-45 management port and the RJ-45 console port on the rear, the USB port on the front and the reset pinhole

power-input.description: the AC inlet of the built-in power supply

rj45.description: 48 PoE+ 10/100/1000BASE-T ports labelled 0 to 47 in four shells of six columns. The even ports are on the upper row

status-leds.description: SYS, MST and CLD chassis lamps (Tables 27 to 30)

uplink.description: Two SFP+ uplink ports labelled 2 and 3, 1 GbE or 10 GbE, in one column of two. The rel-pos carries the printed number

uplink-leds.description: A Link Activity lamp and a Status lamp for each uplink port, triangles in the band between the two cage rows (Table 33). Link Activity is steady with a link and blinking with traffic. Status shows speed: steady 10 Gbps, blinking 1 Gbps

vcp.description: Two SFP+ Virtual Chassis ports labelled 0 and 1, 1 GbE or 10 GbE, in one column of two. They are bracketed by a rounded outline

vcp-leds.description: A Link Activity lamp and a Status lamp for each Virtual Chassis port, triangles in the band between the two cage rows (Table 33). Link Activity is steady with a link and blinking with traffic. Status shows speed: steady 10 Gbps, blinking 1 Gbps

name: ex4000-48p

airflow.note: Table 20, Figure 30 and the cooling section - front to back (air out), the three fans at the rear. The datasheet gives 28 CFM.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Table 20 and Table 21 - the switch has an internal power supply (fixed PSU) and three inbuilt fixed fans with front-to-back airflow; the guide's system overview says the EX4000 switch models have inbuilt fixed fans and power supply units. The guide gives no replacement procedure for either, and no part number. They are part of the chassis and not bays and not components.

chassis.note: Table 21 and Table 26 - height 1.71 in (4.34 cm), width 17.36 in (44.10 cm), depth 11.97 in (30.40 cm), weight 10.8 lb (4.9 kg). The datasheet (specifications) gives the same width, height and depth and a system weight of 4.84 kg; the guide's chassis weight 4.9 kg is carried because Table 26 is the table of chassis weights. The width of 441.0 mm is the metal between the bracket fold lines: the photograph shows no ears and the jack pitch closes on the registry at that width.

color.note: median of the bare face between the logo zone and the first jack shell in the front photograph, #7d838e (the rear plate reads #858c96). Sampled from a studio photograph, whose white balance may differ from the metal. The numerals are the photograph's orange, #f3855a.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The drawing (Figure 15) and the photograph agree on what is on the face. They disagree on the lettering. The photograph prints the port numbers in orange on this PoE+ model and the drawing in black, and the photograph prints EX4000 PoE+ with PoE+ in orange. The drawing draws a round lamp before each of SYS, MST and CLD where the photograph shows none. The photograph of the real device wins for the lettering and the drawing for the lamps. The Juniper logo and the driven by Mist AI line are not drawn: a logo-zone is reserved.

ears.note: The guide's quick-start topic says the two-post rack mounting kit EX-RMK (Table 5, provided) ships in the box with brackets that bolt flush with the front, and the mounting topics give a 2 in. recessed position with the 2-in. recessed front-mounting brackets of the four-post kit EX-4PST-RMK (Table 5, orderable; also a flush four-post mount). The enhanced toolless four-post kit JNP-4PST-RMK-1U-E (orderable) is a further kit. The recess is 2 in. (50.8 mm). No figure measures a bracket fold line, so only the recess has an at (the flush at: 0 is the datum of the face), and the kits are not listed under kits in this slice: they are named here and not modelled as kind kit contracts.

earthing.note: The Connect to Power topic and Figure 16 - a two-hole protective earthing terminal on the rear panel, secured with two M5 x 10 mm screws with washers (not supplied) and a lug on 6 AWG wire. The holes are drawn as decor.

front-layout.note: estimated - Figure 15 and the front photograph at 4.231 px/mm. The 48 jacks stand in four shells of six columns and two rows: the first cell at 11.2 mm, the column pitch 13.97 mm and the shell step 87.8 mm (6 x 13.97 plus a 3.98 mm gutter, from the shell edges at 95.7, 183.5 and 271.3 mm); the rows are 14.3 mm apart (shell top 10.3 mm, bottom 35.7 mm) and the upper row is turned 180 so that its latch and lamps face up, as the photograph shows. The two SFP+ columns abut on the registry's 14.25 mm pitch from 365.2 mm, in two stacked rows on the jack rows, the lower row turned 180 so that both latches face the band between them. The vent fields, the status pill, the USB port and the reset pinhole are read off the photograph.

guide-faces.note: The guide has flat drawings of the front (Figure 15) and rear (Figure 16) and no top, bottom or side elevations; the isometric views are not used.

port-lamps.note: Figures 22 to 26 and Tables 32 and 33 - each RJ-45 jack has a Link Activity lamp at one corner and a Status lamp at the other; the common/rj45-ganged-eth@1 housing carries both. Each SFP+ port has a Link Activity lamp and a Status lamp, the triangles in the band between the two cage rows. The photograph shows them as white triangles in the order down, up, down, up across a column, and the order of the EX4100 (down arrows for the lower port, up arrows for the upper one) is carried; the guide does not say which triangle is which lamp, so that order is estimated. The Status lamp's colour shows speed (Table 32), so its states are not expressible as one vocabulary here (see gaps).

port-numbering.note: The photograph and Figure 15 print 0 and 1, 2 and 3, up to 46 and 47 under the column pairs, each number followed by its triangle (an up triangle after the even number and a down triangle after the odd one), so the upper jack of a column is the even port. The four SFP+ cages are printed 0 and 1 inside a rounded outline (the Virtual Chassis ports) and 2 and 3 outside it (the uplink ports), with the same triangles. Port numbers are as printed on the metal, from 0. The guide gives no interface names for the EX4000 (the hardware guide names none), so none is recorded.

power.note: Table 34 - input 100 to 127 VAC at 12 A or 200 to 240 VAC at 7.5 A, 50 to 60 Hz. Table 35 - system budget 75.05 W, PoE budget 740 W, total 815.05 W. The datasheet's Table 2 gives a maximum system power consumption, input power without PoE, of 71 W; the two are different measures (a budget and a maximum) and both are recorded. The cord is a C13 coupler (power cord topic).

rear.note: estimated - Figure 16 and the rear photograph at 4.28 px/mm. From the left: the RJ-45 management port over the RJ-45 console port in one housing, printed MGMT and CON with a triangle each, three round exhaust fans (34.5 mm across, 46 mm apart, centred 57.4, 103.3 and 149.5 mm), a lighter plate with the two-hole protective earthing terminal and the earth symbol, a round hole for the power cord retainer (callout 5) and the AC inlet in a black housing with its rating printed under it. Four screw heads sit along the lower edge. The photograph shows three fans with their rotors visible, as the drawing does.

scale.note: Gate 1 on the front photograph (2100 x 517 px): the body is 1866 px across (117 to 1983) and its face is 184 px high (163 to 347), against 441.0 by 43.4 mm: 4.231 px/mm across and 4.24 down, so the photograph is near-orthographic and is read at 4.231 px/mm. The ganged jack pitch then reads 59.0 px = 13.95 mm, the registry's 13.97 mm, on a quantity the scale never saw. The guide's flat drawing (Figure 15, 3300 x 1014 px) was checked the same way and does not pass: its body is 3226 px by 320 px (aspect 10.08 against 10.16) but its jack pitch is 99.2 px, 13.5 mm, so its ports are drawn about 3.5 percent close. The drawing is used for what is on the face and for the callouts, and the photograph for positions. The rear photograph (2100 x 501 px) was shot larger: its body runs from 120 to 2008 px, so it reads at 4.28 px/mm between its own edges. The rear positions are taken at that scale and not at the front's.

sources.note: EX4000 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2026-01-20 (261 pages; PDF created 2026-01-20; fetched from https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4000/ex4000.pdf, which answered): Table 3 (models), Figure 15 and Figure 16 (the EX4000-48P front and rear panels, flat drawings g023279 and g023280), Tables 20 and 21 (cooling, power and the physical specifications and ports), Table 26 (chassis), Tables 27 to 33 (the lamps), Table 34 (input), Table 35 (PoE budget), Table 5 (mounting kits) and the mounting topics. EX4000 Line of Ethernet Switches Datasheet, Juniper Networks (PDF created 2025-05-28, 14 pages; https://www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/ex4000-line-of-ethernet-switches-datasheet.pdf): Table 1 (the SKUs), Table 2 (maximum system power without PoE), the specifications and the ordering information. Juniper's image-library photographs ex4000-48p-front-high.jpg and ex4000-48p-rear-high.jpg (from https://www.juniper.net/us/en/company/images/image-library-logos-and-product-photos/products/ex4000-48p.html, 2100 px wide, straight on). The guide prints no terms of use; the image-library page prints none either. Nothing of any of them is copied here, since every face is drawn new from measurements. No Visio stencil and no 3D model of the EX4000 is held or published; the intake folder for Juniper EX and QFX was not available to this work and no held photograph, stencil or model was used. End of life was searched on 2026-10-23 and no Juniper notice for the EX4000 was found, so the lifecycle is recorded as none announced.

status-block.note: estimated - Figure 15 callouts 3, 4 and 5 and the photograph. The three chassis lamps SYS, MST and CLD sit in a rounded pill at the top right; the guide's drawing puts a round lamp before each legend, and the photograph shows the legends only, so the lamps are drawn 2.6 mm before each legend. The pill is read at 396.0 to 424.7 mm and 4.6 to 11.1 mm. Tables 27 to 30 give the lamp meanings; the CLD blink patterns are in another document and are not stated here.

usb-reset.note: estimated - Figure 15 callouts 6 and 8. The USB 2.0 Type-A port (white tongue, USB-A in the same drawing) is read at 399.4 to 413.0 mm across and 29.1 to 35.3 mm down on the photograph, with the USB symbol below it, and the reset pinhole (callout 6, with the reset symbol below) at 431.3 mm by 34.0 mm. The claim code label (callout 7) is a QR code printed at the right of the face in the drawing and is absent from the photograph, so it is a region and not a part.
